desc: A framework for evaluating RAG pipelines with metrics like faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision and recall. Provides reference-free evaluation and integrates with tracing.
examplePrompt: Evaluate our support bot RAG pipeline on 200 FAQ queries. Run faithfulness and answer relevancy, break down by topic, and recommend top 3 retriever or prompt changes with expected impact.
features: Reference-free metrics for faithfulness and answer relevancy
Context precision and recall for retriever tuning
Integrates with LangSmith, Phoenix, and custom tracers
Dataset generation and synthetic test set creation
CI-friendly evaluation runners with regression alerts
longDesc: RAGAS gives teams a repeatable methodology to measure RAG quality without human labels. It ships metrics for faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall, and context entity recall, plus tooling to run evaluations over datasets and CI. Use it to compare retrievers, chunking strategies, and prompts with statistical confidence, and to catch regressions before production.
name: RAGAS: Structured RAG Evaluation
prompt: You are a RAG Evaluation Engineer. Design evaluation sets, run RAGAS metrics, and interpret faithfulness, relevancy, and retrieval scores to guide retriever and prompt changes. Report statistically significant wins and regressions.

desc: A programming framework for building and optimizing LM pipelines. Replace manual prompt tweaking with declarative modules and automatic compilers like MIPRO and GEPA.
examplePrompt: Build a DSPy pipeline for customer ticket classification into 8 intents. Define Signature, collect 200 labeled examples, optimize with MIPROv2, and report accuracy uplift vs baseline prompt.
features: Declarative Signatures and Modules for LM programs
Optimizers like MIPROv2 and GEPA for automatic prompt/weight tuning
Built-in metrics and evaluators for iterative improvement
First-class support for RAG, agents, and multi-stage pipelines
Reproducible experiments with caching and tracing
longDesc: DSPy treats LM calls as modules and optimizes them with compilers. You declare signatures and modules, then DSPy searches over prompts and weights to maximize a metric on your data. It enables reproducible, testable pipelines for RAG, agents, classification, and extraction without brittle string prompts. Teleprompters like MIPROv2 and GEPA automate optimization.
name: DSPy: Programming—Not Prompting
prompt: You are a DSPy Architect. Build LM programs as composable modules with signatures, define metrics, and run optimizers to improve performance. Prefer code over prompt strings and iterate with data-driven evaluation.

desc: A framework for building stateful, multi-actor LLM applications as graphs. Adds persistence, human-in-the-loop, and time travel to agent workflows.
examplePrompt: Design a LangGraph workflow for invoice processing: extract fields, validate with ERP, request human approval on low confidence, and post to accounting. Include persistence and retry logic.
features: State graphs with cycles and conditional edges
Built-in persistence and checkpointing for memory
Deployable with LangGraph Server and LangSmith observability
longDesc: LangGraph models agents as nodes in a state graph with durable checkpointing. It supports cycles, branching, subgraphs, and interrupts for human review. Built-in persistence enables memory, resumability, and time travel debugging. Use it to orchestrate tools, sub-agents, and human approvals in production-grade workflows.
name: LangGraph: Stateful Agent Orchestration
prompt: You are a LangGraph Orchestrator. Design agent workflows as state graphs with nodes for tools and sub-agents, add persistence and interrupts, and ensure fault-tolerant execution with observability.
